complex-qcqp-form: Section II.A, p.2, Eq. (1): the paper defines the complex QCQP in homogeneous form and says each A_i is Hermitian but possibly indefinite.
variational-algorithm-definition: Section II.B, p.2: the paper defines a variational algorithm as the quotes and surrounding paragraph state.
ansatz-setup-simulation: Section III.A and Fig. 1, p.2: the paper states its ansatz gates and that Fig. 1 is the one used in its numerical simulation.
complex-amplitude-encoding: Section III.A, p.2, Eqs. (3) and (4): the paper defines the amplitude encoding and the normalization parameter eta.
real-probability-encoding: Section III.A, pp.2 to 3, Eq. (5): the paper defines the probability encoding and notes the non-negative variables.
primal-dual-ipm-classical-part: Section III.B, p.3: the paper states the classical optimizer it uses and that it rests on second-order gradients.
quantum-computed-quantities: Appendix B, p.8: the paper states what the quantum side supplies and that IPOPT performs the optimization. The experiments are simulations (Section III.A).
eta-numerical-derivative: Section III.B, p.4: the paper states how it computes the derivative with respect to eta.
mu-update-rule: Section III.B, p.4, Eq. (14) and Algorithm 2: the paper defines its own update rule for mu.
opf-formulation-simplified: Section IV.A and Appendix B, pp.4 and 7: the paper states the OPF formulation (Eq. 16) and that it simplifies it by setting the ranges of Re S^G and Im S^G to [0, 1] (the interval is in the passage, not in the quotes).
opf-instance-generation: Appendix B, pp.7 to 8: the three generation rules are listed (uniform [0,1] loads, random connected graph, uniform [0,1] admittances).
maxcut-comparison-setup: Section IV.B and Appendix B, pp.5 and 8: QAOA by the Qiskit implementation, p = 4, l = 5, maximal degree d = 5 are stated. The value says 'an example graph', which matches the text.
qcqp-random-instances: The reader's correction is right. Appendix B, pp.7 to 8: Max-Cut graphs come from G(N,P) with N = 16, P = 0.25, with no connectivity stated. Only the OPF graphs are stated to be connected. The paper states its own instance generation.
hhl-goal-log-time: Introduction, p.1: the paper defines the task HHL addresses (solve Ax = b in time logarithmic in n). Stated as the goal, not as an achieved result.
braket-page-snapshot-2026-footer: The footer text is verbatim at the end of the page text. The page text has no effective date for its prices (no 'as of' or 'updated'). The value claims only the footer and that absence, so it is a statement of what the captured page carries. A copyright year alone does not date the prices.
braket-simulator-instance-price-tables-n: The text carries unrendered placeholders: {regionSelector}, {bulkPriceOf!...} for simulator, Standard, Compute Optimized and Accelerated instance tables, and {priceOf!...} for the SSD storage price. This settles what the captured text does and does not contain. The quote shows the simulator case; the other cases are in the text.

theory_low.monte-carlo-estimator: Algorithm 1 is a procedure the paper describes. It gives no proof that the estimator is unbiased and no variance or sample bound. The value claims the method estimates the form, which the paper does not prove.
theory_low.nonneg-reduction-no-loss-of-generality: A two-line argument with Eq. (6), not a stated theorem with a proof. It does not treat how the normalization of Eq. (5) interacts with the doubled variables. An author claim.
theory_low.polylog-parameters: A scaling argument in prose, Section III.A, p.3. No theorem. It does not show how many layers reach the optimum, so n ~ polylog(N) is an author claim.
theory_low.perturbed-kkt-mu-contraction: Section III.B, p.3 and Appendix A: a description of a cited classical method [13]. No convergence proof, and none for estimates with quantum noise. A cited result.
theory_low.circuit-depth-formulas: Appendix B, p.8: the depth formulas 4l+2 and p(d+1) are stated with no derivation or reference. An author claim.
